title: Creator Spirit, by Whose Light
description: Creator Spirit, by Whose Light in Tonic Solfa to SELENA, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: John Dryden wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 76 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Divine Spirit implored”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SELENA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Cre-a-tor Spir-it, by whose light The sleep-ing worlds were called from night! Come, vis-it ev-ery pi-ous mind, Come, pour thy joys on hu-man kind; From sin and sor-row set us free, And make us tem-ples wor-thy thee.

lines: The sleeping worlds were called from night!
Come, pour thy joys on human kind;
From sin and sorrow set us free,
And make us temples worthy thee.
Plenteous in grace descend from high,
Our frailty help, our vice control,
Thou ruler of our secret soul!
And, lest our feet should haply stray
Protect and guide us in the way.

licence: Public domain: John Dryden died in 1700.
credits: Words by John Dryden (1631–1700), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SELENA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
